pr_title: fix(rust, python): respect `null_on_oob=False` in `list.take` when pa…
pr_body:
…ssed a single index

Attempts to fix #10079

There was a fast path check for `len == 1` which dispatched to `lst_get()` but this does not take `null_on_oob` into consideration.

I have just removed the fast path check/branch and defaulted to always dispatching to `lst_take()`

issue_context.title: `null_on_oob` set to False in `list.take` with single indices doesn't return error
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Reproducible example

```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "a": [[1, 2, 3], [], [None, 3], [5, 6, 7]],
        "b": [['2'], ['3'], [None], ['3','Hi']],
        
    }
)
print(df.select(pl.col("a").list.take([999], null_on_oob=False)))

shape: (4, 1)
┌───────────┐
│ a         │
│ ---       │
│ list[i64] │
╞═══════════╡
│ [null]    │
│ [null]    │
│ [null]    │
│ [null]    │
└───────────┘

print(df.select(pl.col("a").list.take(999, null_on_oob=False)))
shape: (4, 1)
┌───────────┐
│ a         │
│ ---       │
│ list[i64] │
╞═══════════╡
│ [null]    │
│ [null]    │
│ [null]    │
│ [null]    │
└───────────┘
```


### Issue description

Null_on_oob set to False doesn't work when you pass a one integer wrapped in a list as indices. Same thing happens when you only pass a single integer (which also isn't mentioned in type hints that it accepts an integer).

### Expected behavior

```python
print(df.select(pl.col("a").list.take([999], null_on_oob=False)))
```
```python
ComputeError: take indices are out of bounds
```

comments:
Looks like there is a fast path check if the length is 1 and it dispatches to `lst_get()` instead of `lst_take()`

https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/fdbdd1c75c5376f7c26d5bbefc3b941a69edefe2/polars/polars-lazy/polars-plan/src/dsl/function_expr/list.rs#L229-L237

I think the single integer may fall under the type hint of `Expr`

review_comments:
You can keep the `fast_path` but set this condition

```
if idx.len() == 1 && null_on_oob
```
Thanks @ritchie46 - should have been able to figure that one out, d'oh.
